info.title: romulus
info.description: DBA as a service: versioned Postgres schemas, diffs and collaborative drafts.

get.summary:
The IdP's redirect back: exchanges the code, verifies the ID token,
upserts the user and starts a session. Requires a verified email.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: Set by the IdP instead of `code` when sign-in did not happen.

303.description: Signed in: to the `next` of the sign-in, with the session cookie. Otherwise to `/app/signin?error=…`

get.summary:
Starts signing in: redirects to the IdP's authorization endpoint (code
flow, PKCE S256, state, nonce).

parameters.name: next
parameters.description:
Where to land afterwards: a path under `/app`. Anything else is
ignored (the app's home instead).

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.description:
`select_account` asks the IdP which account to use even when one is
already signed in there ("switch account").

parameters.name: login_hint
parameters.description:
The address to sign in with (an invitation's): the IdP pre-fills it,
or offers to create the account. Anything not shaped like an email
is ignored.

303.description: To the IdP; or to `/app/signin?error=sso_unavailable` when it is unreachable

post.summary:
Ends the session (idempotent: an expired one is fine) and clears the
cookie. The web app then navigates to `redirect_url` to end the IdP
session too.

403.description: Missing CSRF header or foreign Origin

get.summary: What the sign-in page can offer.

post.summary:
Imports migration files as versions, from CI: the API token's database.
See the module documentation.

parameters.name: database_id
parameters.description: The database's id (its settings show it)

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Read the files as this tool's; detected from them when absent.

parameters.name: append
parameters.description:
Import even though the database has versions that were not
imported: the imported ones continue the numbering.

parameters.name: dry_run
parameters.description: Replay without storing anything (a CI check).

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: The name of a single SQL text sent as the body (`alembic.sql`).

requestBody.description: The migration files: a multipart form of files (named by their path), a zip, or one SQL text

200.description: Nothing new (`unchanged`), or a dry run that replayed (`checked`); with `Accept: application/x-ndjson` (recommended for CI: no proxy times out), the progress, one `ImportEvent` per line, blank lines keeping the connection alive, the last one `done` or `failed`

409.description: `has_versions` (pass `append=true`), `migration_changed`, `migration_out_of_order`, `concurrent_import` (another import of the database runs, or this one still does)

503.description: `unavailable`: the sandbox is down or busy; nothing stored

post.summary: Pushes a version: remus JSON or SQL. See the module documentation.

parameters.name: database_id
parameters.description: The database's id (its settings show it)

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: What changed, in a line, e.g. the commit subject.

requestBody.description: remus JSON (`remus -f json`), or SQL DDL

503.description: `unavailable`: SQL could not be compiled now; nothing stored

get.summary:
Reads a version back: by number, or the latest. Tokens with the `full`
scope only.
Liveness and database reachability, for compose healthchecks and CI.

200.description: The API and its database are up

get.summary:
What an invitation link invites to, and whether the viewer (signed in or
not) can accept it. Anyone holding the link may look.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The token from the invitation link

post.summary:
Joins the organization with the invited role. The caller must be signed
in with the invited email, verified by the IdP.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The token from the invitation link

get.summary: The signed-in user.

401.description: `unauthorized`, or `session_expired` when the cookie's session is gone

get.summary: The organizations the caller belongs to, by name.

post.summary: Creates an organization; the caller becomes its admin.

get.summary: One organization the caller belongs to.

404.description: No such organization, or not a member

patch.summary:
Renames an organization, moves it to another slug, or changes how many
approvals publishing needs. Admins only.

get.summary: The organization's databases, most recently active first.

404.description: No such organization, or not a member

post.summary: Creates a database (with no version yet). Developers and admins.

422.description: `validation`, `details` names the field; `major_unavailable`: this server has no sandbox for that Postgres major

get.summary: One database.

delete.summary:
Deletes a database: it disappears from the organization, its versions
are kept but unreachable, its API tokens stop working, and its slug can be
used again. Developers and admins.

patch.summary:
Renames a database, moves it to another slug, or changes its
description. Developers and admins.

get.summary: The database's audit events, newest first. Developers and admins.

post.summary:
Compiles SQL without storing anything: its errors, or what it would
change against the latest version. Developers and admins.

get.summary: Compares two versions: what changed from `from` to `to`, three ways.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The version compared from: the left side, `before` in the diff.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description:
The version compared to: the right side, `after`. May equal `from`
(nothing changed), or be older (the diff then reads backwards).

400.description: `bad_request`: a number that is not one

404.description: `not_found`: no such database, or no such version

get.summary:
The open drafts of a database, most recently edited first, with who has
each open.

post.summary:
A new draft from the latest version, ready to edit: no form, renamed
later if wanted. A schema draft by default; with `{"mode": "migration"}`,
a migration from the latest version, written from scratch.

requestBody.description: Optional: a schema draft without one

get.summary: One draft (published ones too: the editor says what became of them).

delete.summary: Deletes an open draft. Whoever has it open is told and let go.

409.description: Published drafts stay with their version

patch.summary: Renames an open draft; everyone in it sees the new name at once.

post.summary: Approves the draft's SQL as the caller reviewed it.

403.description: `edited_draft`: they edited it, someone else approves; `editors_unknown`: a developer or admin, on a draft whose editors are unknown

503.description: The draft could not be loaded

409.description: `draft_published`: its approvals are the version's now

get.summary: The migration publishing the draft now would call for.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description:
The migration tool: its file names, transactions and down migration.
`plain` when absent.

parameters.name: concurrently
parameters.description:
Build indexes on existing tables `CONCURRENTLY`, outside the
transaction (their own files where the tool needs it).

parameters.name: name
parameters.description:
The description in file names (made file-name safe); by default the
target version's message, or `v4_to_v5`.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description:
The first file's version, where the tool numbers its migrations:
Flyway's `V<version>` (digits and dots; by default the target
version's number), or the number other tools put first (digits: a
golang-migrate sequence like `000042`; by default the time,
`YYYYMMDDHHMMSS`). Files after it take the next ones.

parameters.name: sha256
parameters.description:
What the person reviewed (the publish preview's `sha256`, or a live
compile's SHA-256 of the SQL; in migration mode it covers the base
too: `compile::input_hash`): the migration of exactly that, or 409
`draft_changed`. Required: a migration is never of a text unseen.

409.description: `draft_published`: its version has the migration now; `draft_changed`: not the text reviewed (`sha256`); `stale_base`: update the draft first

post.summary: Switches the draft between schema mode and migration mode.

409.description: `draft_changed` (it kept changing: try again), `draft_busy` (being published or updated), `draft_published`

422.description: `compile_failed` (`details.diagnostics`): the SQL has errors, so there is no migration to start from; or the migration does not apply to the current base, so there is no schema to go back to. `unrepresentable` (`details.objects`): no SQL romulus can keep compiles back to the schema the migration made

get.summary: The diff publishing would create, for the confirm dialog.

post.summary: Publishes the draft as the next version.

409.description: `draft_changed` (review again), `stale_base` (update the draft first), `draft_published`, `draft_busy` (someone else is publishing it)

422.description: `compile_failed`: the SQL does not compile (`details.diagnostics`); `unrepresentable`: in migration mode, no SQL romulus can keep compiles back to the schema (`details.objects`)

429.description: `rate_limited`: the checks publishing compiles (migration mode) count against the compile limits

get.summary:
Up to when the caller read each thread of the draft (threads never
opened are not listed).

put.summary: Marks a thread of the draft read up to `at` (never back).

404.description: No such draft, or no such thread in it

post.summary: "Request review": the drafts list shows the draft waits for one.

delete.summary: The draft no longer waits for a review.

post.summary: Rewrites the draft's SQL in canonical form.

409.description: `draft_changed` (it kept changing: try again), `draft_published`, `draft_busy` (being published), `migration_mode` (the draft is edited as a migration)

422.description: `compile_failed` (the SQL has errors, `details.diagnostics`), `tidy_unsafe` (the canonical form would change the schema)

post.summary: Brings the latest version into the draft: see the module documentation.

409.description: `draft_published`, `draft_busy` (being published or updated), `draft_changed` (rewritten meanwhile, try again)

503.description: The draft could not be loaded

parameters.name: filename

409.description: `has_versions` (pass `append=true`), `migration_changed`, `migration_out_of_order`, `concurrent_import` (another import of the database runs, or this one still does)

post.summary:
Reads and plans the files, runs nothing: what an import of them would
do. Developers and admins.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Read the files as this tool's; detected from them when absent.

parameters.name: append
parameters.description:
Import even though the database has versions that were not
imported: the imported ones continue the numbering.

parameters.name: dry_run
parameters.description: Replay without storing anything (a CI check).

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: The name of a single SQL text sent as the body (`alembic.sql`).

requestBody.description: The migration files: a multipart form of files (named by their path), a zip, or one SQL text

422.description: `invalid_migrations` (no migration found, two with one version, a malformed file), `invalid_file`, `validation`

put.summary:
Moves the database to another Postgres major, once its latest version
compiles there. Developers and admins.

409.description: `latest_changed`: a version arrived meanwhile; check again

422.description: `incompatible_major` (`details`: `MajorCheck`): the latest version does not compile there; `major_unavailable`: this server has no sandbox for it; or `validation`

post.summary:
Compiles the latest version on another major, without changing
anything: what moving the database there would meet. Developers and
admins.

422.description: `validation`: not a supported major; `major_unavailable`: this server has no sandbox for it

get.summary: The migration from one version to another, as statements and files.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The version the database is at.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The version to migrate it to. May be older than `from` (a rollback).

parameters.name: format
parameters.description:
The migration tool: its file names, transactions and down migration.
`plain` when absent.

parameters.name: concurrently
parameters.description:
Build indexes on existing tables `CONCURRENTLY`, outside the
transaction (their own files where the tool needs it).

parameters.name: name
parameters.description:
The description in file names (made file-name safe); by default the
target version's message, or `v4_to_v5`.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description:
The first file's version, where the tool numbers its migrations:
Flyway's `V<version>` (digits and dots; by default the target
version's number), or the number other tools put first (digits: a
golang-migrate sequence like `000042`; by default the time,
`YYYYMMDDHHMMSS`). Files after it take the next ones.

400.description: `bad_request`: a number that is not one, an unknown format

404.description: `not_found`: no such database, or no such version

get.summary: The database's live tokens, newest first.

post.summary: Creates a token and answers its secret, once.

delete.summary: Revokes a token: it stops working at once.

get.summary: The database's versions, newest first.

post.summary: Uploads SQL as the next version. Developers and admins.

503.description: `unavailable`: the compiler is down; nothing was stored

get.summary:
The database's removed versions, most recently removed first. Developers
and admins.
One version: its model, source, layout and author.

The migration a version was written as (a draft in migration mode
published it), to read again or download.

404.description: No such version, or it was not written as a migration

post.summary: Hides a version: see the module documentation. Admins.
Brings a removed version back, within [`RESTORE_DAYS`] days. Admins.

get.summary: One version's model as SQL, JSON, DBML and Mermaid.

The version's discussion: its draft's review, frozen, then the threads
started on its page; oldest first.

post.summary:
Starts a thread on the version, pinned to a table, a column, a point of
the graph or a statement.
Replies in a thread.

delete.summary:
Deletes a comment: the caller's, or anyone's for developers and admins
(recorded in the audit log); the thread goes with its last one.

204.description: Deleted (with the thread, when it was its last comment)

patch.summary: Edits one of the caller's comments.

put.summary: Marks a thread read up to `at` (never back: an older `at` changes nothing).

post.summary: Reopens a resolved thread (anyone in the organization).
Resolves a thread (anyone in the organization).

get.summary: Opens a draft live: the y-sync protocol over a websocket.
get.description:
Members only (reviewers watch: their document updates are dropped).
Messages: y-sync (sync, awareness) plus server events (tag 100, see the
`ServerEvent` schema). Close codes: 1012 server restarting, 4000 too
slow, 4001 membership changed, 4002 no answer to pings (reconnect);
4401 session ended, 4404 draft deleted, 4413 draft too large (do not).

404.description: No such draft, or not a member

409.description: The draft is published: open its version instead

get.summary: Pending invitations, newest first, expired ones included. Admins only.

post.summary:
Invites an email address with a role and answers the one-time link.
Inviting an address that already has a pending invitation replaces it
(the old link stops working). Admins only.

delete.summary: Revokes a pending invitation: its link stops working. Admins only.

get.summary: Everyone in the organization, by name. Any member may see who else is.

delete.summary:
Removes a member. Admins may remove anyone; any member may remove
themselves (leave). The last admin cannot go (409 `last_admin`). Closes
the member's live connections.

patch.summary:
Changes a member's role. Admins only; the last admin cannot be demoted
(409 `last_admin`). Closes the member's live connections.

get.summary:
The Postgres majors a database can target, and whether this server
compiles each one now (the major picker, the settings).

already_member.description: The caller was a member already; nothing changed.

ActivityPage.description: A page of events, newest first.

next_before.description: Pass as `before` for the next page; `null` on the last one.

oneOf.description: A table (or view): `schema.name`.

statement.description:
The head of the statement it was written above, when that is not
the table's `CREATE` (an index, a comment…): where the SQL pane
shows it.

oneOf.description: A point of the graph's canvas, in graph coordinates.
A statement about no table (a type, an extension…), by its head.

Anchor.description: What a thread is pinned to.

ApiToken.description: An API token, without its secret.

created_by.description: Who created it; `null` once their account is gone.

last_used_at.description: The last request it authenticated; `null` if never used.

name.description: What it is for: "GitHub Actions", "remus on prod".

sha256.description:
SHA-256 (hex) of the SQL the person reviewed: an approval is of one
text.

oneOf.description: Moved relative to the other attributes, as for columns.

AttributeChange.description:
A change to one attribute of a composite type.

Every variant carries the old value as `before` and the new one as
`after`.

AuditActor.description:
Who did something: their name now, or as it was once their account is
gone.

AuditApprover.description: One approval, as it was when the draft was published.

AuditDetails.description:
What an event says beyond who, when and which version; the fields its
action has.

approvals.description: The approvals it had, and how many the organization required.

approved_by.description: Who approved the text published, when.

authors.description: Whose they were, by name as it was (comments deleted).

draft_id.description:
The draft published (approvals overridden), or whose discussion
lost comments (comments deleted).

excerpt.description: The beginning of the first one (comments deleted).

from.description: The approvals required before and after a change.

message.description: The version's message (versions removed, restored, purged).

thread_id.description: The thread a deletion was in (comments deleted).

oneOf.description: Who did it; `null` for what romulus did itself (the purge).

reason.description: Why, as they wrote it (removals, overrides).

sso.description: Single sign-on is configured (Zitadel is provisioned).

Author.description: Who made a version: a person (uploads, drafts) or an API token (pushes).

Category.description:
What [`Summary`] counts. Partitioned tables count as tables; an entity whose
kind changed counts under its new kind.

against.description:
The version it was compared with; `null` when there is none yet (the
summary then counts what the SQL creates).

summary.description: `"3 tables added, 1 changed; 1 enum changed"`, or `"no changes"`.

unchanged.description:
The model is the latest version's: uploading it would add a version
identical to it.

Code.description: Why a [`Diagnostic`] was raised. Serialised in `snake_case`.

oneOf.description: As `format_type` prints it.

`type_schema.type_name`, with `[]` for an array: reported instead
of [`ColumnChange::Type`] when the type prints the same but is
another type (`email` from another schema on the search path).

Same type text, different kind of type (a domain replaced by an
enum of the same name).

Default expression. For a column generated on both sides the
expression is reported as [`ColumnChange::Expression`] instead.
Generation expression of a column generated on both sides.

The column moved relative to the others. Only for real moves: an
insertion before a column does not move it (positions are compared
through the longest common ordering of the shared columns).

ColumnChange.description:
A change to one column.

Every variant carries the old value as `before` and the new one as
`after`.

ColumnDiff.description:
A column. Columns are listed in table order: by their smallest position on
either side, then their largest, then name, which reads naturally and does
not depend on which side is old.

definition.description:
Type and clauses as in `CREATE TABLE`, without the name:
`bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY NOT NULL`.

CompileReport.description: A dry run: whether the SQL compiles, and what it would change.

oneOf.description: When it compiles: the difference with the latest version.

diagnostics.description: Errors (when it does not compile), then notes, located in the text.

CompileState.description: A compile's outcome, as everyone in the draft receives it.

CompilerStatus.description: What the health check reports about a major's compiler.

CompositeChange.description:
A change to a composite type other than its attributes.

Every variant carries the old value as `before` and the new one as
`after`.

oneOf.description:
`pg_get_constraintdef`, compared with whitespace outside quotes
ignored and reported raw. Also reported when only a structural
field behind the same text differs (columns, target, actions,
deferrable).

ConstraintChange.description:
A change to one constraint.

Every variant carries the old value as `before` and the new one as
`after`.

kind.description: The new kind, or the old one when the constraint was removed.

pg_major.description:
The Postgres major it targets; 17 when not given. Changed later with
`PUT …/major`.

slug.description:
Lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens, at most 63 characters,
not one of the organization's own pages.

CreateDraft.description: How to start a draft (no body: a schema draft).

mode.description:
`migration`: written as a migration from the latest version, from
scratch. `schema` when absent.

slug.description:
Lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens, at most 63 characters,
not one of the app's own routes.

url.description: The one-time link to send to the invitee. Shown only now.

CreatedToken.description: A token just created: the only time its secret is shown.

secret.description: `rom_…`, for `Authorization: Bearer`. Not stored: copy it now.

CurrentUser.description:
The signed-in user, from the session cookie. Every endpoint that needs a
person takes it (or [`super::Member`], which includes it).

Rejects with 401 `unauthorized` without a cookie, 401 `session_expired`
with a cookie whose session is gone, and 401 `unauthorized` for any
request with `Authorization: Bearer`: API tokens are not people, and a
bearer request never falls back to the cookie (see `crate::csrf`).

Database.description: A schema kept in romulus, as its organization's members see it.

last_activity_at.description: When something last happened: the newest version, or an edit.

oneOf.description:
The newest version; `null` before the first upload or push (or
once every version is removed).

missing.description:
Numbers below `latest`'s that have no version: removed, or purged
30 days after (the history skips them).

next_number.description: The number the next version gets: numbers are never given twice.

pg_major.description:
The Postgres major its schema targets: its SQL compiles on that
major, its migrations are generated for it.

versions.description: How many versions it has (removed ones not counted).

Diagnostic.description:
One message about the SQL, located in the text the user wrote (never in
the prepared script the sandbox ran).

code.description: Stable: the web app branches on it.

hint.description: Postgres's `HINT`, or ours: what to do about it.

message.description: One sentence, Postgres's own message for [`Code::Sql`].

oneOf.description:
Where in the text. `None` only for problems with the whole text (too
large, sandbox unavailable).

statement.description:
Index of the statement it is about, in [`crate::ParsedSql::statements`]
order when the text parsed, else in source order.

oneOf.description:
`CHECK (…)` clauses, sorted. The catalog's constraint names are not
in the model, so checks compare by text, whitespace outside quotes
ignored.

DomainChange.description:
A change to a domain.

Every variant carries the old value as `before` and the new one as
`after`.

Draft.description: A draft, as the database page and the editor show it.

base_removed.description:
Its base version was removed (it is stale: "Update draft" moves it
onto the latest version left).

base_version.description: The version it started from; `null` when the database had none.

oneOf.description: `null` once their account is gone.

mode.description: What it is edited as: the schema SQL, or a migration from its base.

next_version.description: The number publishing would give it (numbers are never given twice).

present.description: Who has it open right now.

published_version.description: The version it became, once published.

stale.description:
Someone published since the draft started, or its base version was
removed: publishing it needs "Update draft" first.

pg_major.description: The Postgres major the draft compiles on (its database's).

DraftMode.description:
What a draft is edited as (`draft_mode`): one source of truth at a time
(docs/MVP.md "Review round 1", item 2).

DraftReview.description: Where a draft's review stands, as the drafts list shows it.

approvals.description:
Approvals that count now: of the SQL as it is, by members who did
not edit it.

oneOf.description: The editors asked for a review.

required.description: Approvals publishing needs (the organization's setting); 0: none.

oneOf.description: Row level security enabled.
Row level security forced on the table owner too.
`PARTITION BY` clause, without the keywords.

A view's `SELECT`, as `pg_get_viewdef` prints it. Compared with
whitespace outside quotes ignored, since Postgres majors indent it
differently; reported raw.
Relations a view reads from, sorted.

EntityChange.description:
A change to an entity's own attributes.

Every variant carries the old value as `before` and the new one as
`after`.

EntityDiff.description: A table, view, materialized view or foreign table.

changes.description: Changes to the entity itself. Empty when added or removed.

columns.description:
Every column of an added or removed entity; the added, removed and
changed ones otherwise. In table order (see [`ColumnDiff`]).

constraints.description: By name, like the next three.

kind.description: The new kind, or the old one when the entity was removed.

lines.description: One human-readable line per change, ready for a change list.

partitions.description:
Partitions of a partitioned table, at every level (a sub-partition is
not an entity, so its own partitions are listed here too), by schema
then name.

sql.description:
Table, sequences it owns, partitions, foreign keys, indexes, row level
security and comments; or the view.

EntityStatus.description:
One graph node: the entity's status and that of every part it has on
either side. Foreign keys are the graph's edges. Columns, constraints,
indexes and policies are keyed by name; partitions (every level under this
entity) by schema, then name.

EnumChange.description:
A change to an enum other than its labels.

Every variant carries the old value as `before` and the new one as
`after`.

labels.description:
Every label of an added or removed enum; the added, removed and moved
ones otherwise. Ordered like [`ColumnDiff`]s.

details.description: Structured context, e.g. per-field validation messages.

ExtensionChange.description:
A change to an installed extension.

Every variant carries the old value as `before` and the new one as
`after`.

sandbox.description:
The default major's SQL compiler (17): `ok`, `unavailable` (starting,
or the sandbox is down) or `off` (no sandbox configured). Not part of
the status: the rest of the API works without it.

sandboxes.description:
Every supported major's compiler, by major (`"15"`…`"18"`), as
`sandbox` says it: a database compiles on its own major's.

IgnoreReason.description: Why a file is not a migration.

IgnoredFile.description: A file left out, and why.

ImportError.description: An error, located in its file.

line.description: Where in the file (`path`), 1-based; `null` when unlocated.

oneOf.description: The files, planned: what will be replayed.

Other imports are replaying: this one waits for its turn
(organizations take turns).

Every migration ran once in the sandbox: they replay; versions come
next, one per migration.
A migration's model was read.

number.description: The version number it will get.

oneOf.description: The import finished (the last line).

The import stopped, nothing stored (the last line): 422
`import_failed` (`details`: `ImportFailure`), 409, 503…

ImportEvent.description: One line of an import's progress (`Accept: application/x-ndjson`).

ImportFailure.description: Where a failed import stopped (`details` of 422 `import_failed`).

index.description: Its position among the planned migrations.

ImportPreview.description: What importing the files would do; nothing run yet.

detected.description: The format they look like (`format` unless one was asked for).

first_number.description: The number the first of them would get.

format.description: The format the files are read as.

ignored.description:
Files that are not migrations (down migrations, READMEs, the tool's
own files).

needs_append.description:
The database has versions that were not imported: the import needs
`append=true`, and the imported ones come after them.

new.description: How many versions the import would create.

oneOf.description:
Why the import would be refused as it is (`migration_changed`,
`migration_out_of_order`, `too_many_migrations`, `import_failed`
for a syntax error); `null` when it can run.

migrations.description: Every migration of the files, in order.

changes.description: What it changed, against the version before it: `"2 tables added"`.

status.description:
`new` (created by this import, or would be in a dry run) or
`imported` (already, untouched).

version.description: Its version number (`null` in a dry run).

oneOf.description:
`pg_get_indexdef`. Also reported when only the unique or partial
flag behind the same text differs.

IndexChange.description:
A change to one index.

Every variant carries the old value as `before` and the new one as
`after`.

Invitation.description: A pending invitation (its link is never shown again).

expired.description: The link no longer works; inviting the address again makes a new one.

oneOf.description: `None` once that admin's account is deleted.

InvitationPreview.description: What an invitation link invites to, for its landing page.

email.description:
The invited address: who has to be signed in to accept. Only while
the link can still be used; a used or expired link no longer says.

oneOf.description: The viewer's role when `status` is `already_member`.

InvitationStatus.description: Where the viewer of an invitation link stands.

LabelDiff.description:
One enum label. `changed` means moved: its order relative to the labels
present on both sides changed, which matters because enums compare by
declaration order.

LiveStatus.description: Where a draft is in its life, as the people in it see it.

MajorCheck.description: Whether the database's latest version compiles on another major.

against.description:
The version compiled: the latest. `null` when the database has none
(nothing to check: it may move).

against_major.description:
The major that version was compiled (or pushed) on; `null` when its
model does not say.

oneOf.description:
When it compiles: how its model reads on `pg_major` against the
version's (`no changes`, most often).

compiles.description:
It compiles on `pg_major`, or there is no version: the database may
move there.

diagnostics.description: Errors (when it does not compile), then notes, located in `sql`.

sql.description:
The SQL compiled, when it does not compile (the errors' lines are
its): the version's source, or its model as SQL.

marks.description:
Where the statements with a hazard are (with their comments), for
highlighting.

path.description:
Relative to the tool's migrations folder: `20261016093000_add_invoices.sql`,
`20261016093000_add_invoices/migration.sql`.

MigrationFormat.description:
The migration tool an imported version came from (`migration_format`):
`romulus_sandbox::import::Format` (whose tools are
`romulus_migration::Format`'s), under the same wire names (a test keeps
them in agreement).

MigrationHazard.description: What a statement risks, beyond changing the schema.

MigrationMark.description: Lines of a file holding a statement with a hazard.

MigrationSection.description: The parts of a migration, in order.

MigrationStage.description: When a statement runs relative to the migration's transaction.

MigrationStatement.description: One SQL statement of a migration.

alternative.description:
SQL to run instead, when this statement is half of a likely rename
(a `RENAME` keeps the data a drop and an add would lose). Files show
it commented out.

destructive.description: `hazard` is `deletes_data` or `can_fail`: existing data is at stake.

oneOf.description:
What running it can do beyond changing the schema; `null` when
nothing.

note.description:
What a reviewer should know: why it is there, what it can do to
existing rows, how to do it more safely.

section.description: The part of the migration it belongs to, for headings.

sql.description: One statement, ending with `;` (it may span lines).

MigrationStatementKind.description: What a statement does, for grouping and icons.

MigrationStatus.description: Where a migration stands against the database's imports.

MigrationWarning.description: Something about the migration as a whole that a reviewer must know.

object.description:
The object it is about, schema-qualified and unquoted
(`public.users`, `public.mood`), when it is about one.

Org.description: An organization, as one of its members sees it.

approvals_required.description:
Approvals publishing a draft needs, from members who did not edit
it; 0: none (pushes and imports are never gated).

OrphanPartitions.description:
Partitions whose chain of parents reaches no entity in either schema: the
root table was left out of the model (a schema filter that kept a
sub-partition's schema but not its root's), or the model was written by
hand. They are matched like any partition and described here instead of
under an entity.

sql.description:
Every orphan partition of each side as `remus-sql` renders it; `null`
on a side with none, and on both sides when nothing changed.

oneOf.description: Attached to another table of the same tree.

`FOR VALUES …`, or `DEFAULT`. A `null` bound means `DEFAULT` too
and never differs from it.

`PARTITION BY …` of a partition partitioned in turn (`null` when
it is a leaf).

PartitionChange.description:
A change to one partition.

Every variant carries the old value as `before` and the new one as
`after`.

PartitionDiff.description: A partition, matched by its own schema and name.

definition.description:
`FOR VALUES …` or `DEFAULT`, then `PARTITION BY …` when the
partition is partitioned in turn.

parent.description:
The table it is a partition of (the entity, or a partition that is
itself partitioned): the new one, or the old one when removed.

PgMajor.description: A Postgres major romulus compiles on: 15, 16, 17 (the default) or 18.

PlannedMigration.description: One migration of the files, in order.

errors.description: Syntax errors (new migrations only): the import would stop here.

id.description:
The tool's version (`20240101120000`, `1.2`, `blog.0002_post_slug`),
or the file name without `.sql` for plain folders: what later
imports match on.

line.description: The line of `path` where it starts (exported files hold several).

name.description: The version's message: the file (or folder) name.

skipped.description: What will not be replayed (new migrations only).

version.description: The version it became, when imported already (or removed since).

oneOf.description: Sorted; empty means `PUBLIC`.

PolicyChange.description:
A change to one row level security policy.

Every variant carries the old value as `before` and the new one as
`after`.

definition.description:
What follows `CREATE POLICY name ON table`:
`AS RESTRICTIVE FOR SELECT TO reader USING (…)`.

Position.description:
A 1-based line and column. Columns count Unicode scalar values, which is
what an editor's "Ln 3, Col 7" shows for text without combining marks.

Positions.description:
0-based index in the old and the new list, `null` on the side the item is
absent from. Every item carries both, moved or not.

PostgresMajor.description: A Postgres major romulus compiles on, as this server runs it.

server_version.description:
The exact version compiles run on (`17.11 (Debian …)`), once its
sandbox answered.

status.description:
Whether its compiles run now: `ok`, `unavailable` (starting, or its
sandbox is down) or `off` (this server has no sandbox for it).

Present.description: Someone who has a draft open right now.

editing.description: They may edit (developer or admin); otherwise they watch (reviewer).

PublishApprovals.description: What publishing would need, for the publish dialog.

approved_by.description: Who approved the SQL previewed, without having edited it.

can_override.description: The caller may publish without them, saying why (admins).

message.description: What changed, in a line (at most 1000 characters).

override_reason.description:
Publish without the approvals the organization requires, saying why
(admins; the audit log keeps it).

sha256.description: The `sha256` of the preview the person confirmed.

PublishPreview.description: What publishing the draft now would create.

approvals.description: The approvals the organization requires, and who approved this SQL.

base_model.description: The base version's model, for drawing the diff.

diagnostics.description: Errors that prevent publishing (then no diff), then notes.

oneOf.description:
What changes against the base version (against nothing when there is
none); `null` when the SQL does not compile.

migration.description: Migration mode: the migration the version will keep.

mode.description: What the draft is edited as: its SQL, or a migration from its base.

model.description: The model the version would have.

number.description: The number the new version would get.

sha256.description:
What was previewed (`compile::input_hash`: the SQL; in migration
mode the migration and the base it applies to): send it back to
publish exactly this.

stale.description: Someone published since the draft started: "Update draft" first.

version.description: The version created, or the latest one when unchanged.

at.description: The newest comment the person saw.

reason.description:
Why, for the audit log and whoever restores it (1 to 1000
characters).

RemovedVersion.description: A removed version, until it is purged.

oneOf.description: `null` once their account is gone.

restorable.description: It still can be (`restorable_until` is to come).

restorable_until.description: It can be restored until then, and is purged soon after.

ReviewApproval.description: One member's approval, as the people in the draft see it.

ReviewRequest.description: A draft's editors asked for a review ("Request review").

Role.description: A member's role in an organization (`member_role`).

SchemaDiff.description:
Everything that differs between two schemas, matched by schema and name:
a rename is a removal plus an addition.

Lists hold only what was added, removed or changed. [`SchemaDiff::status`]
is the total view (every object of either side, unchanged ones included)
for highlighting a graph.

entities.description:
Tables, partitioned tables, views, materialized views and foreign
tables, by schema then name. Partitions are listed under the entity
their chain of parents leads to, not here.

SchemaMigration.description: A migration, as statements and as the files of one tool.

archive.description: What the files download as together: `<version>_<name>.zip`.

destructive.description: How many statements delete data or can fail on existing rows.

files.description: The files to put in the tool's migrations folder, in order.

from.description:
The version migrated from; `null` for nothing (a draft of a database
without versions).

pg_major.description: The Postgres major it is written for: the database's.

statements.description: In order; the same whatever the format.

to.description:
The version migrated to (for a draft, the number publishing it would
give).

warnings.description:
What to know before running it (a column that ends up elsewhere, a
possible rename, a type recreated…).

oneOf.description:
The first event after connecting: how the server treats this
connection.

read_only.description:
Document updates from this connection are dropped (reviewers,
and everyone once the draft is no longer open).

role.description: The connection's role in the organization.

oneOf.description:
The latest compile of the draft's SQL. Sent to everyone after each
compile, and to each connection when it joins.

diagnostics.description:
Errors (when `failed`), then notes. Spans count UTF-16 code
units in `utf16_start`/`utf16_end`, like `Y.Text` in the browser.

model.description:
The model when `ok`. When `failed`, the last model that compiled,
sent only on joining (others already have it); keep showing the
previous one when absent.

schema_sql.description:
In migration mode, with `model`: the schema it is, as SQL
(read-only: the migration is the source). Absent otherwise.

sha256.description:
Hex SHA-256 of the SQL compiled. A client whose text hashes the
same can place `diagnostics` as they are; otherwise a newer
compile is on its way.

oneOf.description:
The draft switched modes (docs/MVP.md "Review round 1", item 2):
the doc's `meta.mode` changed in the same transaction as its texts.

To one connection: its last edit changed the text that is not the
source in `mode` (sent before it saw a switch), and was undone.

The draft's status changed (publishing started, failed or
succeeded; the draft was deleted).
The draft was renamed.

The database has a new version (another draft was published): if
it is not this draft's base, publishing now needs "Update draft".

Someone moved the database to another Postgres major: the draft
compiles on it from now on (a compile follows).

An admin removed a version: if it is this draft's base, publishing
now needs "Update draft" (onto the latest version left).
An admin restored a removed version.

Approvals and the review request (`collab::review`): sent on joining
and whenever they change (an approval, an edit resetting them,
someone becoming an editor, the organization's setting).

approvals.description:
Approvals of the SQL as it is now, by members who did not edit
it, oldest first: these count.

editors.description: Who changed the SQL: they cannot approve it.

editors_unknown.description:
Edited before romulus recorded editors: only reviewers (who never
could edit) may approve it.

outdated.description: Approvals of an earlier text: an edit since reset them.

oneOf.description: The review the editors asked for, if they did.

required.description: Approvals publishing needs (the organization's setting); 0: none.

oneOf.description:
The server could not store some edits (its database failing): they
live in the open tabs only.

To one connection: what became of its comment operation `id`
(`MESSAGE_COMMENT`). When `ok`, the doc's update came first.

The draft was updated to a newer version ("Update draft"): its base
is now `version`; `conflicts` blocks are left to resolve.

ServerEvent.description: A message only the server sends (tag 100 on the websocket), as JSON.

Sides.description:
The same thing on both sides, `null` where it does not exist.

For an object it is the DDL `remus-sql` renders for it alone (statements
separated by blank lines, ending with a newline), so the web can show the
two side by side. For a part of an object it is the one-line definition:
a column's type and clauses, a constraint's `pg_get_constraintdef`, an
index's `CREATE INDEX`, a policy's clauses after `ON table`, a partition's
bound.

redirect_url.description:
Where the browser goes next: the IdP's logout (which comes back to
the sign-in page), or the sign-in page itself.

SkipReason.description: Why a statement is not replayed.

SkippedStatement.description: A statement not replayed, located in its file.

Span.description:
A range of a SQL text, `start..end`, in bytes, UTF-16 code units and
line/column.

end.description: Byte offset just past the last character.

start.description: Byte offset of the first character.

to.description: Where `end` is (the position just past the range).

utf16_start.description: `start` in UTF-16 code units: a JavaScript string index.

Status.description:
Where an object, or a part of one, stands between the old and the new
schema.

StatusMap.description:
Status of every object on either side, unchanged ones included.

Schema-qualified objects are nested by schema, then name, both unquoted
exactly as in the model: `status.entities["shop"]["orders"]`. Nesting keeps
keys collision-free without making the web reproduce Postgres's quoting
rules (a flat `schema.name` key cannot tell schema `a.b` + table `c` from
schema `a` + table `b.c`). Extensions are database-wide, keyed by name.

Summary.description: Counts per category, and the same as one sentence.

counts.description: Categories with at least one change, in [`Category`] order.

text.description: `"3 tables added, 1 changed; 1 enum changed"`, or `"no changes"`.

color.description:
A color name (`stone`, `red`, `amber`, `green`, `teal`, `blue`,
`violet`, `pink`); the web app draws an unknown one as `stone`.

members.description: Qualified names of the tables in it.

ThreadRead.description: Up to when the caller read a thread.

thread.description: The thread's id in the draft's doc.

changed.description: Whether the SQL changed (false: it was tidy already).

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the SQL as Tidy left it.

TokenScope.description: What an API token may do (`api_token_scope`).

TypeKind.description: `pg_type.typtype` of a column's type, as a word.

slug.description: Changing it changes every link to the database (pushes use its id).
Changing it changes every link to the organization.

base_version.description:
The version the draft is based on now (`null`: the database has
none).

changed.description: Whether anything changed (already on the latest version: nothing).

conflicts.description: Conflict blocks in its SQL now: publishing waits until none is left.

diagnostics.description:
Migration mode: the migration's errors on the new base, located in
it (absent when it still applies, and in schema mode).

message.description: What changed, in a line (at most 1000 characters).

sql.description: The schema as SQL DDL, at most 1 MiB.

VersionApproval.description: An approval of the draft a version was published from, as it was then.

author_name.description: Their name when they wrote it.

approvals.description:
Who approved the draft it was published from, when the organization
required approvals (`drafts::approvals::freeze`); oldest first.

layout.description:
Table positions and groups, keyed by qualified name (empty until a
draft arranges them).

oneOf.description: The migration file it was imported from (origin `import` only).

model.description: The remus model (`remus_core::Schema` as JSON), canonical.

source.description:
What was uploaded or pushed, verbatim: SQL, remus JSON, or the
migration's up SQL for imports.

written_migration.description:
Published from a draft in migration mode: the migration it was
written as is at `…/versions/{number}/migration`.

diff.description:
From `from`'s model to `to`'s: the change list, the summary and the
status of every object for the graph.

layout.description:
Where the union's tables sit: the newer version's positions and
groups; the older one's positions for tables the newer did not place
(the ones it removed, say), each in its old group if the newer one
still has it, or in its old group alone if not.

models.description: Both models: the graph draws their union, styled by `diff.status`.

sql.description:
Both models as SQL, rendered the same way whatever their source (an
upload's text or a push's JSON): canonical order, and the newer
version's header on both, so a line diff of the two shows only what
the schema changed.

VersionLayout.description: Where tables sit, and their groups.

layout.description: Top-left corner of each table in graph coordinates, by qualified name.

VersionMigration.description: The migration an imported version came from.

id.description: The tool's version of it, or its file name for plain folders.

path.description: The file, relative to the folder imported.

skipped.description:
What was not replayed (`SkippedStatement[]`, lines in the version's
`source`: the migration's own text).

VersionOrigin.description: How a version came to be (`version_origin`).

VersionPage.description: A page of versions, newest first.

next_before.description: Pass as `before` for the next page; `null` on the last one.

VersionPostgres.description:
The Postgres a version was compiled on (uploads, drafts, imports: the
sandbox of its database's major) or pushed from (remus JSON: the real
server). Versions keep it when their database moves to another major.

database_major.description: The major its database targeted when it was created.

major.description: `server_version`'s major; `null` when it does not start with one.

other_major.description:
Pushed from a server on another major than its database targeted
then: the history flags it, and offers to move the database.

oneOf.description: `null` once the person's account or the token is gone.

message.description: What changed, in a line; `null` when none was given.

number.description:
1, 2, 3… per database, never given twice (a removed version leaves
its number unused).

written_migration.description:
Published from a draft in migration mode: the migration it was
written as is at `…/versions/{number}/migration`.

VersionTexts.description: A version's model in every format the viewer shows.

sql.description:
The source for SQL versions; rendered from the model for pushed JSON
and imported migrations.

VersionThread.description: A thread of a version's discussion.

created_by.description: Who started it (`null` once their account is gone).

frozen.description:
From the review of the draft the version was published from, as it
was then: read-only.

read_at.description: Up to when the caller read it (`null`: never opened).

WrittenMigration.description:
The migration a version was written as, in a draft in migration mode:
from the version before it (nothing, for a first version) to it.

from.description: The version it migrates from; `null` for a first version.

sql.description: The migration, as written (data statements included).
